\]
The area of the parallelogram formed by these vectors can be found using the cross product $\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}$. The magnitude of this vector gives us the area.

First, compute the cross product:
\[
\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v} = \begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\
3 & 1 & -2 \\
1 & -3 & 4
\end{vmatrix}
= \mathbf{i} \left(1 \cdot 4 - (-2) \cdot (-3)\right) - \mathbf{j} \left(3 \cdot 4 - (-2) \cdot 1\right) + \mathbf{k} \left(3 \cdot (-3) - 1 \cdot 1\right)
\]
\[
= \mathbf{i} (4 - 6) - \mathbf{j} (12 - 2) + \mathbf{k} (-9 - 1)
\]
\[
= -2 \mathbf{i} - 10 \mathbf{j} - 10 \mathbf{k}
\]
\[
= \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -10 \\ -10 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

Next, we find the magnitude of this vector to get the area:
\[
\left\| \mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v} \right\| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-10)^2 + (-10)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 100 + 100} = \sqrt{204} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 51} = 2\sqrt{51}.
